header.title: Government Certified Providers
header.sub: Where to find the official, government-published list of accredited service providers or Peppol-ready software for each country — verified directly against the relevant authority's own site, not a third-party summary.

statusBanner.text: This is a starting set of verified links, not a complete map of all 48 tracked jurisdictions. Every link below was checked directly against the named government/authority's own website. Several countries in this tracker don't run a public accreditation registry at all — see the note in Section 3 before assuming one exists.

sec1.heading: Same idea, different names
sec1.intro: Every country below runs a version of the same concept — a government-recognised list of software or intermediaries you can safely rely on — but each one uses its own term for it.

card1.body: Used in the UAE. The intermediary that validates and transmits your e-invoices over the Peppol network on your behalf.

card2.body: Used in Mexico. The third party authorised by SAT to stamp (timbrar) your CFDI and give it legal validity.

card3.body: Used in Peru. An OSE validates your invoice with the same legal authority as SUNAT itself; a PSE signs on your behalf using its own certificate.

card4.body: Used in India. A licensed intermediary providing the software/API layer that connects a taxpayer to the GSTN.

card5.title: Peppol Service Provider / Access Point
card5.body: Used in Malaysia, Singapore, Australia, and any other Peppol-based market. An accredited Access Point connects your business to the shared Peppol network.

sec2.heading: Verified official links, by country
sec2.intro: Click through to the authority's own page — always cross-check a specific provider's current status there directly before signing anything, since these lists change.

table.uae: Ministry of Finance's register of pre-approved / accredited e-invoicing Service Providers (ASPs)
table.mexico: SAT's register of Proveedores Autorizados de Certificación
table.peru: SUNAT's official padrón (registry) of authorised OSE and PSE providers
table.india: GSTN's list of licensed GST Suvidha Providers
table.malaysia: MDEC's (Malaysia's Peppol Authority) register of accredited Peppol Service Providers
table.singapore: IMDA's list of authorised Access Point providers and InvoiceNow-Ready solutions
table.australia: The ATO's (Australian Peppol Authority) register of accredited Peppol service providers
table.france: The DGFiP's list of registered Plateformes Agréées (formerly PDP)

sec2.franceNote: France's exact list sits within the DGFiP's broader impots.gouv.fr site rather than one fixed, stable URL we could verify with full confidence — search "liste des plateformes agréées" directly on that site for the current version.

sec3.heading: Where this pattern doesn't apply
sec3.intro: Several major markets in this tracker simply don't run a public provider-accreditation registry at all — worth knowing so you don't go looking for one that doesn't exist.

card1.body: KSeF and SDI are both direct government platforms — any compliant software can connect via the published API/schema, with no formal "accredited intermediary" layer to certify against.

card2.body: Taxpayers self-certify as authorised issuers directly with the tax authority (SEFAZ, SII); there's no equivalent PAC/OSE-style third-party accreditation model in either country.

card3.body: ZATCA doesn't publish a comparable public list — compliance is a matter of your invoicing system meeting the published technical specification directly, not intermediary accreditation.

sec4.heading: One resource that spans every Peppol market
sec4.body: For any Peppol-based country not yet in the table above — Belgium, Norway, Denmark, and others — OpenPeppol itself (the network's governing body) maintains a single global register of every certified Peppol service provider, searchable by country of legal residence.

card1.title: 🏷️ Understand the vendor categories first
card1.body: "Types of Provider" (under Education) breaks down ERP, Solution Provider, Tax Compliance, Technology, and Consultancy categories before you start browsing government lists.

card2.title: 🗓️ Ready to run a vendor selection?
card2.body: "Preparing for a Mandate" (under Education) walks through how to evaluate and select a provider once you've found the right list.

card3.title: 🌍 Check your country's specific requirements
card3.body: The Deep Dives menu covers exact registration steps, technical specifications, and penalties for each of the 48 jurisdictions tracked here.

card4.title: 📬 This list will grow
card4.body: More countries will be added here as we verify their official sources directly — subscribers get notified when new entries are published.

footer.text: This page links directly to official government and authority sources as verified at the date above, and is provided for general awareness — it is not an endorsement of any specific provider, and inclusion on a government list is not a guarantee of fit for your specific needs. Always confirm a provider's current accreditation status directly on the linked official page before signing an agreement.
